findings.symptom: A frame's rank and cycle scan are seeded from the AUTHORED blockedBy refs, so a reference that crosses an anchor does not resolve in the frame that draws the edge. Reproduced black-box against the BUILT dist (probe-d1.log): case B — outer task T2 blocked by inner B1 draws the edge teamB->T2[board], yet T2 gets depth 0 and ranks [[T1,T2],[teamB]] put T2 in an EARLIER column than the box the line leaves from (a backwards dependency line). Case C — a cross-frame mutual block (T1 blocked by X1 inside G1, X1 blocked by T1) emits both G1->T1 and T1->G1 with cycles: [] so the panel's `dependency cycle: <ids>` warning can never fire. The mirror case (A) and the group->group case (D) are correct, which matches the writer's own scope note.
findings.expected: Rank each frame from the ANCHORED pair set (the from of every pair whose to is the node) while keeping node.dependencies as authored text, and report a cross-frame mutual block as a CYCLE instead of two silent roots (contract Amendment 8 R1; D1's ranking clause: the outer model ranks group pseudo-nodes so external columns stay correct).

findings.symptom: The BUILT-IN nested fixture of the independent oracle gate never produces a group->group edge. The gate's grouped model shows only B1->B2, B1->teamB1, B2->teamB1[derived], T1->T2, T1->teamB, T2->teamB — no frame-to-frame edge — while the model itself does implement the branch (my probe case D yields GA->GB[board]). The branch is therefore asserted only by a package arm, and a regression in it cannot redden `verify-graph-model`.
findings.expected: The gate fixture, its grouped oracle (expectedGroupedModel) and the golden must each demonstrate the group->group attachment the contract names, so the durable gate — not only a package test — can catch a regression (contract Amendment 8 R2; D1 attachment rule 'an edge between two groups becomes group->group').
findings.docSource: .mpd/plans/cellwork-w4-contract.md — Amendment 8 R2 'gate-level group->group proof'; D1 attachment rule

findings.symptom: For a collision between a GROUP id and a task id, the refusal message names the same frame twice: 'the grouping input carries id "G" in the root frame and the root frame; ids must be unique across the whole tree'. The refusal itself is correct and arrives before any model is built, but the message cannot tell a caller which group collided (probe case E2).
findings.expected: Name the two DISTINCT frames that carry the id, so a caller debugging a group-id collision learns the group as well as the task (README 'Ids are unique across the WHOLE tree ... REFUSED with an Error naming both frames').
findings.docSource: packages/mpd-graph-core/README.md — 'Ids are unique across the WHOLE tree'
